title: The homepage greets players with a creator pitch
problem: Under a bright site-wide banner, the first block on the homepage is a creator pitch: "Have a game you'd like to share?" with a "Share your game" button. There is no headline (no h1) telling a player what YouGame is. The first content is "Browse by game" (three ROM base games), followed by "Emulator & ROM hacks".
why_it_matters: Most visitors arrive to play, not to upload. If the first screen speaks to creators, players have to work out the site's purpose on their own, and the games that would hook them sit below the fold.
recommendation: Lead with one player-facing headline as the page's h1 (for example "Play community games, free, in your browser"), with no eyebrow or subtitle, and one featured instant-play game with a big Play button. Keep "Upload" in the header and move the creator pitch to a slim card further down the feed.
agent_prompt: On the yougame.co homepage, replace the top "Have a game you'd like to share?" intro block with a player-first hero. Requirements: (1) an h1 headline stating what YouGame is for players, max ~10 words; (2) no eyebrow label above it and no subtitle under it; (3) a featured game card (cover, title, creator, one stat line, primary Play button) chosen from the current top game that plays instantly in the browser; (4) remove the "Share your game" button from the hero, keep "Upload" in the header nav, and add a compact creator card ("Made a game? Share it" + link to /upload) after the first row of games. Keep existing routes and sort params working. The page must have exactly one h1.

title: One filter row mixes three kinds of filter that all look the same
problem: A single row holds player mode (Single player, Multiplayer), 21 genre chips (cut off at "Shoot…" behind a scroll arrow) and sort (For you, Most played, Newest), all styled as identical pills. Sort sits at the far right after the genre scroller, and two chips are selected at once (All and Most played) with the same black fill.
why_it_matters: When every control looks the same, people can't tell which chips combine and which replace each other, or that the right-hand chips change the order rather than filter. Hiding most genres behind a sideways scroll arrow makes them easy to miss.
recommendation: Give each kind of filter its own control in one bar: a segmented control for sort on the left, a single "Players" dropdown, then a genre row showing the top 6 genres plus "More genres".
agent_prompt: On the yougame.co homepage, restructure the single filter row into three distinct controls in one bar. (1) Sort (For you / Most played / Newest) becomes a segmented control placed first, on the left. (2) Single player / Multiplayer / All becomes one dropdown labelled "Players: All" that keeps the existing ?players= query param. (3) Genres show as chips: the 6 most-used genres plus a "More genres" chip that opens the full list, instead of a sideways-scrolling row. Each control type must look different from the others, and the selected state of each must be announced to assistive tech (aria-pressed / aria-selected). Preserve all existing query params (sort, players, genre).

title: Instant browser games and "bring your own disc" games look the same
problem: Emulator remixes like Project+ need the YG desktop app (Mac with Apple silicon or Windows only) plus the player's own disc image; games like GlobeTap run instantly in the browser. Emulator cards carry a purple "Needs your own copy" badge, but it doesn't mention the desktop app. They also have rich cover art while browser games show plain colour tiles, so the games most visitors can't play right away get the most attention and top the "Most played" order.
why_it_matters: A new player clicks the most popular game, lands on a page whose main button is "Download desktop app", and learns they need a legally obtained Wii disc image. That is a dead end for most first-time visitors and makes the site feel like it doesn't work.
recommendation: Show where each game runs as the card's base colour, not as one more text tag: one colour for "Plays in your browser", another for "Desktop app + your copy", explained once by a small legend above the grid. Add a "Plays in browser" filter that is on by default for first-time visitors, and keep emulator remixes in their own shelf.
agent_prompt: Show where each yougame.co game runs as the base colour of its card instead of a text tag. (1) Derive a runs_in value per game: "browser" for web games in the sandboxed frame, "desktop" for emulator/ROM-hack games that need the YG desktop app and a user-supplied disc image. (2) Tint the card's info area (below the cover art) with one of two background tokens, e.g. --card-browser and --card-desktop, both meeting 4.5:1 contrast with the card text. (3) Remove the per-card "Needs your own copy" text tag. (4) Add one legend above the feed: two swatches labelled "Plays in your browser" and "Desktop app + your copy", with an info tip beside the second explaining that it needs the YG desktop app and your own legally obtained copy of the base game. (5) Add a "Plays in browser" toggle to the filter bar (?instant=1), on by default for visitors who are not signed in and have never opened the desktop app. Colour must not be the only cue for assistive tech: include runs_in in each card's accessible name.

title: Game cards cram too much metadata, and it runs together
problem: Each card stacks a lot: chips over the cover (mode, input type), a "Needs your own copy" badge, a "Runs on your copy of…" line with a mini thumbnail, the creator, live players, rating, total plays and last-active time. Browser-game cards show only some of these, so cards in the same row don't line up.
why_it_matters: When every card carries eight facts, none of them stands out and scanning the grid is slow. Inconsistent layouts make it hard to compare games at a glance.
recommendation: Use one fixed card anatomy: cover, title, creator, and a single stat line in plain text (★ 4.2 · 13.9K plays, or "3 playing now" when live). Where it runs is the card's base colour (see UX-03). Move input type, mode and last-updated to the game page.
agent_prompt: Refactor the yougame.co GameCard component to a fixed anatomy: (1) 16:9 cover image with meaningful alt text (the game title); (2) title, 1 line, ellipsis; (3) creator name, 1 line; (4) one stat line: if live players > 0 show "● N playing now", else show "★ rating · N plays" (omit rating if fewer than 3 ratings); separate values with " · "; (5) no badges or pills on the card; where the game runs is shown by the card's base colour (see UX-03). Remove input-type tags, mode tags and last-active time from the card. Ensure all cards in a row have equal height.

title: Site-wide update banner says "press Play to update" with no Play button
problem: Every page, including browser-game pages and the sign-up form, shows a bright orange bar: "A YG Dolphin update is out: press Play to update." It has no button, no dismiss control and no link, and it refers to an emulator most visitors have never installed.
why_it_matters: A banner that appears everywhere trains people to ignore banners, so real announcements get missed. For new visitors it adds jargon (YG Dolphin) on their very first screen.
recommendation: Only show the update notice inside the desktop app, or on emulator game pages to signed-in users who have used it. Give it a concrete action ("Update now") and a dismiss button.
agent_prompt: Change the global "A YG Dolphin update is out" banner on yougame.co: (1) render it only when the visitor is in the desktop app, or is signed in and has launched an emulator game before; (2) add an explicit "Update now" button that triggers the update (or deep-links to the desktop app) and an icon-only dismiss button with aria-label="Dismiss"; (3) remember dismissal per update version in localStorage; (4) never show it on /login or on web-game pages.

title: Emulator game pages hide the setup steps below the fold
problem: On Project+ the hero is a video with "Not on this computer yet" over it. Below sit a help link, the title, creator, and a row of rating, Save, Community, Share, This is my game and "…". What you actually need (desktop app, a specific Brawl edition, accepted file types) is in a long paragraph further down, with "No copy stored yet" as its status.
why_it_matters: Players can't tell how close they are to playing. "Download desktop app" sounds like the whole story, and only after installing do they find they also need a specific Brawl edition (USA Rev 1 or Rev 2).
recommendation: Put a three-step "Get ready to play" checklist in the hero: 1) Get the desktop app, 2) Add your copy of Brawl (USA Rev 1 / Rev 2), 3) Play. Each step shows done or not done, and the main button always shows the next step.
agent_prompt: On yougame.co game pages for emulator games (games that require the desktop app and a user-supplied disc image), add a "Get ready to play" checklist directly under the title, above the creator row. Steps: (1) "Get the desktop app" — done if the desktop app is detected; (2) "Add your copy of <base game> (<accepted editions>)" — done if a matching verified image is stored; (3) "Play". The primary button label always reflects the first incomplete step ("Download desktop app" → "Add your copy" → "Play"). Show accepted file types in a collapsed "Which files work?" disclosure. Keep the existing requirements panel content but move it into this component.

title: The same things go by different names
problem: Right under the Project+ video, one link says "Trouble with your disc, Orca or a controller? YG Dolphin help", so the emulator gets two names in one line (the banner says "YG Dolphin", descriptions say "Orca", and the help URL is /help/orca). The footer has both "Report a bug" and "Ideas and bugs", and homepage cards say "mods" while game pages say "remix".
why_it_matters: Each extra name is something players must learn. When names don't match, people assume they are different things and search for help in the wrong place.
recommendation: Pick one public name per concept (for example "YG Dolphin" for the emulator, "Remix" for mods, "Feedback" for the ideas/bugs board) and use it everywhere: nav, banners, help URLs and cards.
agent_prompt: Standardise terminology across yougame.co UI copy. (1) Emulator: use "YG Dolphin" in all user-facing copy; keep "Orca" only in developer/architecture docs; add a redirect so /help/yg-dolphin is the canonical help URL and /help/orca 301s to it. (2) Use "remix" everywhere the homepage currently says "mod"/"mods". (3) Rename header "Request feature" and footer "Ideas and bugs" to the same label, "Feedback". Search all templates and string files for each old term and list every change in the PR description.

title: "Upload" drops people on a sign-up wall with no context
problem: Clicking Upload goes to "Create your account". Continue with Apple and Google come first, which is good, but the email path asks for a gamer tag and a choice of 26 avatar icons before email and password. Nothing on the page says what uploading involves or that you'll return to upload afterwards.
why_it_matters: Creators want to know "can I upload my thing, and how hard is it?" before committing to an account. Choosing an avatar first adds a decision that has nothing to do with their goal.
recommendation: Let anyone open /upload and see the three ways to add a game (paste HTML, drop a file, import a link), then ask them to sign in when they submit. On the email sign-up path, ask for email and password first and pick the avatar after sign-up.
agent_prompt: Make /upload on yougame.co viewable without signing in. Show the upload options (paste HTML, drop a file, import a link) and the specs link; let the user prepare their submission, and only require auth when they press Publish (open sign-in in a modal and keep their draft). On the account creation form, reorder to: Continue with Apple, Continue with Google, email, password, gamer tag; remove the avatar picker from sign-up and prompt for it once after first login. Add a line at the top of the auth modal when it was opened from upload: "Sign in to publish your game. Your draft is saved."

title: Accessibility basics are missing: headings, alt text, button labels
problem: The homepage has no h1. Almost every cover image has empty alt text. Carousel arrows are bare "‹" and "›" characters with no accessible label.
why_it_matters: Screen-reader users can't tell what the page is or which game a card is, and they hear "left angle quote" instead of "Previous". Missing headings and alt text also hurt search ranking and link previews.
recommendation: Add one h1 per page, give cover images alt text with the game's title, and label icon-only buttons (Previous, Next, Dismiss).
agent_prompt: Fix accessibility basics across yougame.co: (1) every page has exactly one h1 (homepage: the hero headline; game pages: the game title); (2) every game cover has alt equal to the game title, decorative images use alt=""; (3) carousel arrow buttons get aria-label="Previous" / "Next" and are real

title: Game pages give every action equal weight
problem: GlobeTap's page shows Play, Invite a friend, Follow, Save, Casual, Ranked, Play with a friend, Tournaments, Community, Remix, Share and "This is my game" near the top, plus in-game controls (Pause, Restart, End game) in the page markup.
why_it_matters: When a dozen actions compete, the one that matters (Play) loses emphasis, and rarely used actions like claiming a listing take up prime space.
recommendation: Group actions into three tiers: one primary (Play), a couple of secondary (Invite, Save, Share), and an overflow "…" menu for Remix, Claim this game and Report. Show mode choice (Casual / Ranked / With a friend) only after pressing Play.
agent_prompt: Restructure the action area on yougame.co web-game pages. (1) Primary: a single large Play button. (2) Secondary row: Invite a friend, Save, Share. (3) Overflow menu ("More" icon button with aria-label): Remix, Community, Tournaments, This is my game, Report. (4) Move the Casual / Ranked / Play with a friend choice into a small sheet that opens after pressing Play (default Casual; remember last choice). (5) In-game controls (Pause, Restart, End game) must render only while a game session is active.

title: "How it works" is a manifesto, not instructions
problem: How it works has two headers stacked: the site header, then the page's own "YouGame · For you · How it works · Full guide ↗" bar. The hero is an all-caps eyebrow ("THE FUTURE OF PLAY IS A COMMUNITY EFFORT.") over a manifesto headline, then origin-story cards. The practical steps come later, the developer list starts at "02", and example screens are labelled "illustrative".
why_it_matters: People who click "How it works" usually want to know what to do next. A mission statement first delays the answer, and the numbering gap and mock screens make the product feel unfinished.
recommendation: Open with two short 3-step guides side by side, "To play" and "To share a game", each with one button. Drop the eyebrow labels, move the mission and origin stories below, and fix the numbering.
agent_prompt: Reorder /how-it-works on yougame.co: (1) top section with two columns, "To play" (Pick a game → Press Play → Invite friends; CTA "Find a game" to /) and "To share a game" (Sign up → Paste HTML, drop a file or import a link → Publish; CTA "Share your game" to /upload); (2) move the mission and the three origin-story cards below; (3) remove the all-caps eyebrow labels above section headings ("THE FUTURE OF PLAY…", "OUR MISSION"); (4) fix the developer list so it starts at 01; (5) label the Little World mocks "Coming soon" if the shown features don't exist yet. Also remove the page-level secondary header (YouGame / For you / How it works / Full guide) so only the site header remains; turn its in-page anchors into a short table of contents under the h1 if still needed.

title: Support questions pile up in game comments
problem: Most of the 94 comments on Project+ are support threads: controllers not binding, settings not saving, Linux/Steam Deck support. The developer answers them one by one, and the same questions repeat.
why_it_matters: Players with a problem scroll through long threads instead of finding an answer, and the developer spends time re-answering. Real discussion about the game gets buried.
recommendation: Add a "Known issues & help" panel above comments listing the top problems and their status, with a clear "Report a bug" button. Tag support comments so they can be filtered out of the main discussion.
agent_prompt: On yougame.co game pages, add a "Known issues & help" panel above the comments section. Data model: per game, a list of {title, status: open|fixed|in progress, help_link?} editable by the game owner. Show up to 5 items with status chips and a "Report a bug" button that opens the existing bug report flow pre-filled with the game id. Add an optional "Help" tag on comments and a comment filter "Hide help questions".

title: Internal links wear the "leaves this site" arrow
problem: Links that stay on yougame.co carry the corner arrow ↗ that normally means "opens another site": "Full guide ↗" on How it works, and "See the base game ↗", "See the whole remix tree ↗" and "Community chat ↗" on game pages. Real external links use the same arrow.
why_it_matters: The ↗ arrow tells people a link opens another site. Using it on internal links makes them hesitate, and makes it impossible to tell which links actually leave YouGame.
recommendation: Use ↗ only on links that leave yougame.co. Internal buttons are plain labels with no trailing arrow or chevron.
agent_prompt: Audit all links and buttons on yougame.co. Remove the trailing "↗" (and any trailing → or › chevron) from every link whose href stays on yougame.co. Keep "↗" only on links to other domains, and add rel="noopener" plus a visually hidden "(opens another site)" to those. List every changed label in the PR description.

title: The header is a row of unlabelled icons
problem: Next to search, the header shows seven icon-only buttons: a globe, a palette, a bug, a light bulb, a question mark, a plus and an avatar. None has a visible label, so Upload (the plus) and Feedback (the bulb) are hard to find, and the globe and palette give no hint of what they do.
why_it_matters: Icons without labels make people guess or hover each one. Key actions like uploading a game and sending feedback get missed, and the row reads as clutter.
recommendation: Show text labels for the actions that matter (Upload, Feedback, Sign in) and move rarely used ones (language, theme, help) into the account or overflow menu. Every remaining icon gets a tooltip and an accessible name.
agent_prompt: Rework the yougame.co site header. (1) Keep the logo, search field and account avatar. (2) Replace the icon-only plus and light-bulb buttons with labelled text buttons "Upload" and "Feedback"; when signed out, show a labelled "Sign in" button in place of the avatar. (3) Move the globe (language), palette (theme) and question-mark (help) actions into the account menu (or an overflow "More" menu when signed out). (4) The bug icon becomes a "Report a bug" item in that menu and stays on game pages. (5) Every icon-only control left in the header gets aria-label and a tooltip. Check the header at 1280px and 375px widths; on mobile, collapse labelled actions into the menu.

title: The site copies YouTube's look, not just its layout
problem: The site's stylesheet opens with "Visual language borrowed from YouTube's desktop web app" and uses YouTube's own values: Roboto, #0f0f0f text, #606060 secondary text, 5% black chips, #065fd4 links, a 56px header with a rounded search box and a sticky chip bar. With a red rounded-square logo, the whole site reads as a YouTube skin. YouGame's own touches (the Bricolage Grotesque wordmark, emoji shelf headings, jam gold, the coloured game tiles) are scattered rather than forming a look of their own.
why_it_matters: Borrowing YouTube's layout helps: people already know how to browse a grid of thumbnails with filters and a creator line. Borrowing its identity doesn't. The repo's launch checklist (docs/RELEASE_READINESS.md, Marketing) already says to clear the "YouGame" mark and stop describing the product as "YouTube for games" in public, and a YouTube-looking site works against that. Nothing in the look says "play" either.
recommendation: Keep the layout (thumbnail grid, filter chips, creator byline, related list) and replace the identity layer: a type pairing of YouGame's own (for example Bricolage Grotesque for page and section headings, not only the wordmark), its own accent and selection colour, a cover-art treatment for game cards (see IM-01), and a logo that doesn't read as YouTube's red play button. Define these once as tokens so every page picks them up.
agent_prompt: Propose a visual identity for yougame.co that keeps today's layout but stops looking like YouTube. Work only in the token layer: the :root, dark-mode and [data-theme="dark"] blocks at the top of web/src/app/globals.css and the fonts in web/src/app/layout.tsx. (1) Pick a heading face and a body face (Bricolage Grotesque is already loaded for the wordmark; it can carry page and section headings). (2) Choose an accent and a selection colour that are not YouTube red or black and pass 4.5:1 for text in light and dark. (3) Remove the "borrowed from YouTube" comment and name the new tokens for what they do. (4) Don't change layout, spacing or components. Show before/after screenshots of the home page and one game page in light and dark in the PR, and list every token you changed with its old and new value.

title: Game pages stack a dozen panels and offer two places to start playing
problem: Under the player, a game page can stack a mode pill with its own hint line, the creator row, then the Alpha panel, the base-game panel, Versions, Description, Release notes, the remix panel, Leaderboard, Top players, the gallery and Comments, each as its own full-width block. On desktop the right column has a Play menu (lobby, play with a friend) while the row under the title also has Queue and Play with a friend. The right column then opens with chips (More games, the genre, the mode, From the creator) that repeat what the title area already says.
why_it_matters: With every section given the same weight, the page reads as one long scroll with no shape, and the same job (start playing, with whom) appears in two places that can disagree. Players can't tell what matters, and creators' updates and leaderboards get lost under everything else.
recommendation: One play panel by the player holds every way to start (alone, ranked, with a friend), so the right column no longer repeats it (see UX-10 for the action tiers). Replace the mode row with one line of facts under the title ("Multiplayer · 2–4 players · ★ 4.2 · 12.4K plays"). After a short description, put the rest in tabs: Leaderboard · Versions & remixes · Updates · Comments. Start the right column with a plain "More like this" heading instead of chips.
agent_prompt: Restructure the game page at web/src/app/g/[slug]/page.tsx on yougame.co. (1) Merge the desktop PlayMenu in the right column (.rail) with the play actions in the byline (QueuePicker, PlayWithFriend) into one play panel beside the Player; the rail keeps only related games. (2) Replace the .game-mode row (mode pill + hint) with one meta line under the title: mode, player count, rating, plays. (3) Below the description, render Leaderboard/TopPlayers, the versions panel plus RemixPanel, ReleaseNotes and Comments as tabs ("Leaderboard", "Versions & remixes", "Updates", "Comments"), each tab only when it has content, Comments selected by default; keep the URL hash in sync so #comment-<id> links still open the Comments tab. (4) Replace the rail's chip row with an h2 "More like this". Keep every existing feature reachable. Add strings to web/src/i18n/messages/en.json. Show desktop and phone screenshots before and after.
